Germination of common chickweed

Source: R/data.R
chickweed.Rd

Germination of 200 chickweed (Stellaria media) seeds in one germination test, from a study of chlorsulfuron resistant and sensitive biotypes, recorded in time intervals: an example of time-to-event data (family = "event" of drmTMB).

Usage

chickweed

Format

A data frame with 35 rows and 3 variables:

start

left endpoint of the monitoring interval (hours)

end

right endpoint of the monitoring interval (hours)

count

number of seeds germinated in the interval

Source

Lisa Borggaard (formerly Faculty of Life Sciences, University of Copenhagen); from the package drcData.

Details

200 seeds were placed in Petri dishes in a dark growth cabinet at 5 degrees Celsius, and the germinated seeds were counted and removed at 34 inspection times. Chickweed has dormant seeds, so that the proportion of germinated seeds stays well below 1. The last row, with end = Inf, holds the seeds that had not germinated by the end of the experiment.

References

Ritz, C., Pipper, C. B. and Streibig, J. C. (2013) Analysis of germination data from agricultural experiments. European Journal of Agronomy, 45, 1–6.

Examples

gmod <- drmTMB(count ~ start + end, data = chickweed, model = "loglogistic", family = "event",
               start = c(b5 = 0), fix = c(b5 = TRUE))
# times by which 10%, 50% and 90% of the germinating seeds have germinated
ed(gmod, c(10, 50, 90))
#> Effective dose estimates:
#> 
#>        Estimate Std.Error
#> 10:lf1      176      3.49
#> 50:lf1      196      2.51
#> 90:lf1      218      4.27
# time by which 10% of all seeds have germinated
ed(gmod, 0.1, type = "absolute")
#> Effective dose estimates:
#> 
#>           Estimate Std.Error
#> y=0.1:lf1      196      3.66
